correctness.rationale: The membership of the second-arrival branch is an exact two-colour Pólya urn with uniform terminal size. Conditional on its membership history, the two induced birth-ordered trees have independent uniform parents. The global size-k fringe count decomposes into counts in the two induced trees minus the complement-root indicator. A separately proved insertion recurrence gives mu_k(m), symmetry cancels its two conditioned means, and the remaining indicator produces (2k-n)/(2(n-1)). Exhaustive enumeration of all recursive trees through n=9 and rational recurrence checks through n=120 passed 14728 assertions. The finite checks corroborate rather than replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Primary text materially examined: Holmgren–Janson 2014 Theorems 1.4, 1.13–1.15 and Benkner–Wagner 2022 Lemma 3 concern global fringe statistics; the 2008 earliest paper focuses on phase changes of the same global count, though its entire text was not obtained. Existing published related results concern root degree/leaf count and root attachments/path length, and accessible historical claims concern direct-child degrees vs subtree sizes or global leaf counts. None inspected states or implies the distinguished second-arrival subtree size versus all-size-k fringe-count covariance. This is an originality judgment, not proof of universal uniqueness; explicit residual risks follow.
residual_risks: The complete 2008 Feng–Mahmoud–Panholzer text was not accessible for every appendix and proof; an implicit specialized identity is possible even though the stated object is global fringe-size counts.
Very general multivariate random increasing-tree frameworks might imply the result after additional disaggregation that was not found in the inspected sources.
Semantic search and a restricted literature sample cannot certify exhaustive historical uniqueness.

The 2026 Bäumler–Briend–Jorritsma paper has a similar fringe-size splitting construction; its available excerpts address bounds rather than the exact claimed covariance, but the full original text was inaccessible.

value.rationale: The mixed dependence of early-branch mass and global fringe-size profile is a motivated structural statistic for nonexchangeable increasing trees. The exact all-size regression isolates a single root-boundary term and gives a complete positive/zero/negative sign phase classification at \(n=2k\). The object is a canonical whole profile, not an arbitrary numerical slice, and the result is not a textbook substitution or mere recomputation of the global marginal mean.
